summary: BifrOSt checks a device-owner password at login and unlock (PAM through the root helper) and a lock-screen passcode, but apps get no API for either and there is no biometric support. The app keychain is the only app-facing secret store, and it has no user-presence or biometric access control.

features.note: Wave 2 (theme-02, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No Touch ID, Face ID or fingerprint support in the shell or SDK. Grep for fprint, fprintd, howdy and biometric returns nothing except the keychain doc's gap note (docs/bifrost-ui.md around line 410).

features.feature: Device-owner password or passcode authentication for apps
features.note: Login and unlock check the account password through the root helper (PAM service bifrost-login, faillock). The lock-screen passcode is a salted, stretched hash in passcode.ini. Neither is exposed to apps as an SDK call that asks the user to authenticate.
The Rust shell has no SwiftUI. Only the system login and lock prompts exist; an app cannot show a reusable authentication sheet.

features.feature: Keychain items protected by user presence or biometrics
features.apple: SecAccessControl, kSecAttrAccessControl (Accessing Keychain Items with Face ID or Touch ID)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-01, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Items are readable whenever the shell runs. There is no access control class and no prompt before reading a secret (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Keychain section, parity gaps).

features.feature: Persisted rights and secrets (LARight, LAPersistedRight, LASecret, LARightStore)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-01, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No right or requirement model exists. The keychain stores only generic passwords keyed by (service, account).

features.feature: Authentication requirements and biometry fallback (LAAuthenticationRequirement, LABiometryFallbackRequirement)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-02, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No requirement objects or fallback chain. The only fallback is the password path at login.

features.feature: Key pairs gated by authentication (LAPublicKey, LAPrivateKey)
features.note: Wave 3 (theme-10, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The keychain has no keys or certificates (only kSecClassGenericPassword). No Secure Enclave equivalent is present; the master key is a file on disk (springboard/src/keychain.rs, module comment).
The keychain error type mirrors the SecItem OSStatus codes (DuplicateItem, ItemNotFound, Param, NotPermitted, Io). No LAError codes exist, since there is no LAContext.

features.feature: Biometry type and device state (LADomainState, LAEnvironment, kLABiometryType*)
features.note: Wave 2 (theme-02, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No API reports whether biometrics or a passcode are enrolled, or which biometry type exists. Apps cannot choose a policy from device capability.

features.feature: Companion device authentication (Apple Watch, Vision Pro)
features.note: Tied to Apple-only companion hardware with no BifrOSt counterpart.

gaps: No biometric authentication (Touch ID, Face ID, fingerprint). Nothing in the shell or SDK; fprint, fprintd and howdy are absent.
No app-facing authentication API: an app cannot ask the user for the account password or passcode before a sensitive action (the LAContext evaluatePolicy equivalent).
Keychain items have no access control. Any item an app can read is readable without user presence (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Keychain, parity gaps).
No authentication-gated rights, persisted secrets or key pairs (LARight, LAPersistedRight, LASecret, LAPrivateKey).
No device capability query for enrolled biometry or passcode (LADomainState and kLABiometryType constants).
